default.quote:
If you were a fan of Episode 1 racer, there is not a reason to miss out on this one. Racing is smooth and FAST, using your Ramjet and Afterburner and drifting through a sharp turn that turns the camera instantaneously is the best feeling in a racing game.

It might appear like a very hard game at first, but its also a roguelite game. You can upgrade your speeder to make the next runs easier and different. I had a great time clearing the campaign, can't wait to do it again trying different builds!
default.author: alejandrogaleas

default.quote: Absolutely fantastic! Star Wars: Galactic Racer on PS5 is an incredible experience. Stunning visuals, thrilling races, smooth gameplay, and an amazing Star Wars atmosphere. Pure adrenaline from start to finish! A must-play for racing fans and Star Wars lovers. Highly recommended!
default.author: lagob

default.quote:
This game is perfect!

It had been a long time since I felt motivated to play racing games, as this genre no longer seems to receive the same love and care it used to.

But then, out of nowhere, Star Wars: Galactic Racer arrives... and it's here to stay, ready to earn its place among the greats. Non-stop action and guaranteed fun.

A deeply crafted story mode built around a roguelite system that works flawlessly, with the same concept also making its way into multiplayer. I've barely been able to put the game down when playing with my friends.

An absolute gem.
default.author: Suleh_98

default.quote: Oh how i wish i would love this game more. First the most important thing, SPEED and FEEL: People say it's fast, but i have to disagree. F-Zero, Extreme G, Episode 1 Racer - those games are fast! In Episode 1 Racer for example, you could really see how much scenery you were leaving behind at high speed. This game, on the other hand, only gives you the impression of speed, while the tracks themselves feel small. Then there’s the handling: the racers feel floaty, sloppy and soft to control. I miss the highly precise, sharp-edged handling of the really good old-school sci-fi racing games. Then there are the absurd DESIGN DECISIONS: no split-screen multiplayer, no option to select individual tracks, no time trials, no maps, and the decision to turn the Pod Racers into a separate game within the game. And finally, the TRACKS themselves: there simply aren’t enough of them, and they aren’t particularly creative. Another comparison to Episode I: Racer — there were sandcrawlers on the track, Tusken Raiders shooting at you, traps, and anti-gravity tunnels. Why do the tracks in a Star Wars racing game have to be so boring and unimaginative? Another criticism is the CAMPAIGN. It’s certainly creative, but I don’t need constant story interruptions in an arcade racer. I want to race, not chat with mechanics and other characters. I thought a Star Wars Racer from a Burnout-Team would be my dream game (i loved the Burnout-games!). Now i hope for some patches and updates, because i wont play this game much longer...
default.author: MagMachina

default.quote:
It starts off being a crashfest, but you kinda like it.  Then you sort of start to get it and finally beat the first part of the story and then the game just goes down hill further and further.

it introduced more mechanics that make an already visually challenging game even more so.

the environmental hazards become way over tuned

the AI rubber banding is insane.  they also need seem impervious or invulnerable to environmental hazards that are legal to you.

The menu navigation isn't well designed.  You often can't see what option you have highlighted.  The didn't put a colour around the thing you're on, they just opted to enlarge it 5% bigger than the non selected options.  it's too subtle and visually it just adds another cut to the hundred other cuts of pain the game causes.

I have to admit that when it clicks for a few corners without crashing you do feel **** then you inevitably crash.  or get crashed by the cheating AI, who all seems to just hunt you and not each other. 

Ultimately it's a rage inducing pile of garbage and you should spend your money somewhere else
default.author: OS_Gamer

default.quote: I just recently uploaded the original Podracer game for N64 on my PS5 and was amped to play this. But on extensive play-through, I don't see the difference. If anything the original game has better levels, and 3 times as many characters. The graphics sure r great, but the ability of what there is to do, and without spit-screen, it just lacks any replay-abiltiy for me. And that's saying something after just releasing.

positive.quote: In many racing games, you might eventually feel like a pilot. But only in this one you become a Jedi. It is insane. I can't stop playing it. The sensation is indescribable. This game let the players play the story and feel what it is like to be behind those speed monsters. And when you get to control them, when you are going through those dark tunnels of death at more than 600, 800, 1,000km/h, at night, in a heavy rain, and when only the sudden lightnings briefly show the surrounding and the shapes so you have a millisecond to turn... only then you understand what it is to have the force be with you. This is a masterpiece. This is the best Star Wars game ever made because it is the only one that truly delivers the force. It is also one of the best racing games ever. This is one of my favourite games of all time.

positive.quote: If you ever enjoyed a Burnout game or a Motor Storm game this game is literally that on Star Wars lore world. Must buy.
